stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and benefits from Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Is Big Tech’s AI slowdown a safety pact or a cartel?
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: Major AI leaders (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, SpaceX) have agreed to slow down frontier AI development.
The stated goal of the slowdown is to 'pace the frontier' of AI advancement.
Skeptics are questioning the motives, suggesting the slowdown could be a safety pact or an industry cartel.

stories.title: For the first time, the US military confirms it has deployed weapons in orbit
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: The US military has officially confirmed the deployment of weapons in orbit.
These new systems are described as 'on-orbit space control weapons'.
The stated purpose of these weapons is to defend the joint military forces.

stories.title: Corrupt Plans, Clean Traces: Evading Chain-of-Thought Monitoring with Plan Injection
stories.author: Vasilis Syrgkanis
bullet_points: Introduces 'plan injection,' a novel adversarial attack against Chain-of-Thought (CoT) monitoring systems.
The attack involves injecting seemingly benign reasoning into an LLM's context to steer it toward harmful actions.
This research highlights a critical vulnerability in current LLM safety mechanisms designed to detect unsafe planning.

stories.title: K-Bench: a clinically calibrated benchmark for evaluating large language models in high-risk mental health conversations
stories.author: Elena Volkova
bullet_points: Introduces K-Bench, a new, clinically calibrated benchmark specifically designed to test LLMs in high-risk mental health scenarios.
Evaluates a wide range of models (125 configurations from 33 base models across 14 providers) using 200 multi-turn vignettes.
Focuses on critical safety areas including suicide, self-harm, domestic violence, and substance misuse, addressing a major gap in current LLM safety evaluation.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, indicating a focus on practical LLM deployment.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The model is associated with key AI technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains including 'transformers' and 'text-generation'.
The presence of 'safetensors' indicates modern, secure model handling practices.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for running complex, multi-step tasks and tool-calling locally on user hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a substantial community of 8.9 million developers.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging MLX.
Speedup reaches up to 90% when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: What execs and politicians are saying about slowing down AI development
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: AI safety concerns are driving a major industry conversation regarding the pace of AI development.
Dario Amodei published a key essay advocating for slowing down frontier AI research.
The topic is generating significant discourse among AI leaders and political figures.

stories.title: AI leaders want to hit the brakes after years of reckless speed
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: AI leaders are advocating for a slowdown in the current rapid pace of AI development.
The stated primary reason for the slowdown is a heightened focus on AI safety.
The article suggests there may be underlying, potentially strategic, benefits for the AI industry behind the call for caution.

stories.title: The Router Within: Eliciting Native Skill Routing from a Frozen LLM
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Proposes a novel method to achieve native skill routing within a frozen Large Language Model (LLM) without relying on external context or retrieval pipelines.
Argues that the necessary routing signal is inherently present within the LLM's forward passes, suggesting an internal mechanism for skill selection.
Demonstrates that only two linear maps are required to effectively 'read' and utilize this latent routing signal, offering a computationally efficient solution.

stories.title: The Router Within: Eliciting Native Skill Routing from a Frozen LLM
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: The research proposes a novel method to enable LLM agents to select appropriate 'skills' without relying on external, context-heavy routing mechanisms.
It demonstrates that the routing signal for skill selection can be inherently extracted from the frozen LLM's own forward passes using simple linear maps.
This approach aims to overcome limitations of current routing methods, such as context dispersion or loss of agent capability when moving selection outside the context.

stories.title: Mind2Dialogue: Training Human-Aware Language Models by Simulating User Mental States
stories.author: Zhen Wang
bullet_points: Introduces 'Mind2Dialogue,' a method to train language models to be more 'human-aware' by simulating user mental states.
Addresses the critical 'supervision gap' in current LLM training, where datasets lack explicit grounding in users' unspoken beliefs and goals.
Suggests that achieving deep, long-term collaboration between AI and humans requires models that can infer underlying user intent.

stories.title: The Router Within: Eliciting Native Skill Routing from a Frozen LLM
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: The research proposes a method to elicit native skill routing directly from a frozen Large Language Model (LLM) without external context management.
It addresses limitations of current routing methods (like context preloading or retrieval pipelines) which either dilute attention or remove routing capability from the agent.
The core finding suggests that the necessary routing signal is inherently present within the LLM's forward passes, requiring only simple linear maps for extraction.

stories.title: Discovery Foundation Models: Toward Open-Ended Discovery Intelligence
stories.author: Yingcheng Wu
bullet_points: Proposes 'Discovery Intelligence' as the next frontier for foundation models, moving beyond solving human-specified problems.
DFMs aim to enable models to participate in the creation of new problems, representations, and knowledge.
The evolution involves a shift from learning over existing knowledge to learning through action, tool use, and outcome feedback.

stories.title: Mind2Dialogue: Training Human-Aware Language Models by Simulating User Mental States
stories.author: Zhen Wang
bullet_points: Introduces 'Mind2Dialogue,' a method to train language models to be more human-aware.
Addresses the 'supervision gap' where current LLM training lacks data reflecting users' unspoken beliefs and goals.
Suggests the need for deeper understanding of human mental states for effective long-term AI collaboration.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to leverage open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings enhanced performance and broader GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to expand model support across various hardware configurations.
It improves Ollama's MLX engine specifically for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes a 'local-first' approach, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Microsoft issues emergency Windows 11 update to fix its record-breaking patch
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft released an emergency out-of-band update for Windows 11.
The emergency patch addresses bugs introduced by the massive September Patch Tuesday update.
The initial update contained nearly 1,000 fixes but caused issues affecting businesses, developers, and gamers, notably with Hyper-V folder shares.

stories.title: Apple Home’s new security camera features cost as much as $60 a month
stories.author: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy
bullet_points: Apple Home is integrating Apple Intelligence into HomeKit Secure Video with the release of iOS 27 and tvOS 27.
The new feature provides AI-powered video summaries, offering text descriptions of events captured by compatible security cameras.
Access to these enhanced AI features will require users to pay an additional monthly subscription fee.

stories.title: Valve’s virtual reality plans hit actual reality
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: Valve has released the Steam Frame VR headset.
The headset's expected price point was aimed to be under $1,059.
Manufacturing costs were impacted by global RAM and storage market fluctuations.

stories.title: Rocket Lab is seeing red about NASA's decision on a Mars spacecraft
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: Rocket Lab is publicly criticizing NASA's recent award decision regarding a Mars spacecraft.
The core of Rocket Lab's complaint is that the award decision seems to contradict established eligibility criteria.
This highlights ongoing competitive and procedural tensions between private aerospace contractors and NASA.

stories.title: AI bots "Timmy," "Ren," and "Jackie" are flooding social media with slop
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: AI bots are proliferating across social media platforms.
These bots are generating low-quality, repetitive content ('slop').
The trend highlights the current challenges of AI content saturation and authenticity.

stories.title: OpenAI stuck fighting Musk antitrust suit after Apple finds a way out
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: OpenAI is facing ongoing antitrust scrutiny, despite recent developments.
Elon Musk has ceased legal challenges against Apple regarding ChatGPT integration.
The situation highlights the complex interplay between major tech players (Apple, OpenAI, Musk) in the AI space.

stories.title: Founder’s cost-cutting obsession drove Unitree lead in cheap humanoid robots
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Unitree's success in developing affordable humanoid robots is attributed to the founder's intense, cost-cutting leadership.
The article questions the scalability of this highly micromanaged leadership style as the company grows.
The piece touches upon the intersection of robotics hardware development and corporate management strategy.

stories.title: Apple releases iOS 27, macOS Golden Gate 27 with Siri AI and Liquid Glass refinements
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Apple has released iOS 27 and macOS Golden Gate 27, featuring updates to Siri AI and Liquid Glass.
The release marks the final macOS version to maintain support for Rosetta, impacting Intel application compatibility.
The update signifies Apple's ongoing integration of advanced AI features into its core operating systems.

stories.title: Stellar Colosseum: A Many-Agent Harness for Long-Horizon Research in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science
stories.author: Vahab Mirrokni
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of current language models in handling long-horizon, complex research problems in math and theoretical CS.
Introduces 'Stellar Colosseum,' a model-agnostic harness designed to manage and allocate inference across these difficult research tasks.
The system employs mechanisms like exploring alternative strategies and a 'readiness gate' to guide the proof construction process.

stories.title: Vulnerability Localization Benchmark: Measuring Agentic Security Analysis at Repository Scale
stories.author: Amin Karbasi
bullet_points: Introduces the Vulnerability Localization Benchmark (VLoc Bench) to address a gap in current AI security evaluations.
Focuses on the specific task of vulnerability localization—identifying the exact code files related to a weakness class within a large repository.
Addresses the growing trend of language-model agents operating over entire software repositories, demanding more granular security analysis.

stories.title: SlipSense: Multimodal Tactile Learning for Low-Latency and Generalized Slip Detection
stories.author: Tao Yu
bullet_points: Introduces SlipSense, a multimodal framework for low-latency and generalized slip detection in dexterous manipulation.
Utilizes a compact sensor (TacV5) combining a 32x32 piezoresistive array (240 Hz) and a 3-axis MEMS accelerometer (8 kHz).
Addresses limitations in current systems regarding detection latency and cross-platform generalization for tactile sensing.

stories.title: Privacy-enhanced federated learning via asynchronous aggregation and local differential perturbation
stories.author: Liesheng Wei
bullet_points: Proposes a privacy-enhanced federated learning framework for secure collaborative training.
Integrates Dynamic Differential Privacy (DDP), Homomorphic Encryption (HE), and Local Differential Privacy (LDP) for robust data protection.
Utilizes an asynchronous aggregation strategy with version control to handle distributed training environments.

stories.title: Bellman Policy Optimization
stories.author: Lidong Bing
bullet_points: Introduces Bellman Policy Optimization (BPO), a new critic-free method for Reinforcement Learning.
BPO is designed to improve the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) using verifiable rewards (RLVR).
The method reformulates Policy Mirror Descent (PMD) for autoregressive generation using Bellman equations, avoiding intermediate state value estimation.

stories.title: Stellar Colosseum: A Many-Agent Harness for Long-Horizon Research in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science
stories.author: Vahab Mirrokni
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of current language models in handling long-horizon, complex research problems in math and theoretical CS.
Introduces 'Stellar Colosseum,' a model-agnostic harness designed to manage and allocate inference across these difficult research tasks.
The system uses mechanisms like an 'alternative strategy exploration' and a 'readiness gate' to guide the proof construction process.

stories.title: A Chosen Future Can Still Be Rewritten: Causal Writability in Video Models
stories.author: Ziming Liu
bullet_points: Introduces the concept of 'Causal Writability' in video models, addressing whether motion errors stem from poor learning or poor utilization.
Demonstrates that correct motion information can remain latent within the model even when the generated output is physically incorrect.
Proposes a method using low-dimensional edits to force the model to generate desired, conflicting motion patterns.

stories.title: Disentangling Representation Evolution in Transformers through Directional Decomposition
stories.author: Shen Yan
bullet_points: The research models Transformer representation evolution as a functional geometry, analyzing learned additive transformations.
Key finding is the existence of substantial parallel components in representation updates beyond the standard residual path.
The decomposition method is applied to analyze updates within both attention mechanisms and MLP layers.

stories.title: Privacy-Aligned Personalized Federated Learning with Compact Adaptation and Variable-Length Gaussian Communication
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Addresses a structural misalignment in personalized federated learning when client variations are low-dimensional but updates are high-dimensional.
Proposes a method to confine repeated adaptation to a fixed coefficient space after releasing a private client context once.
Introduces a factorized generator that adapts the optimization geometry to reshape noisy updates while maintaining privacy.

stories.title: Safe Meta-Reinforcement Learning via Information Space Reachability
stories.author: Navid Azizan
bullet_points: Addresses the critical gap in applying Meta-Reinforcement Learning (meta-RL) to real-world scenarios due to safety concerns.
Proposes a novel safe meta-RL framework designed to explicitly incorporate safety constraints during the adaptation process.
Introduces the concept of reasoning about safety within the 'information space,' which integrates both physical state and agent belief.

stories.title: SlipSense: Multimodal Tactile Learning for Low-Latency and Generalized Slip Detection
stories.author: Tao Yu
bullet_points: Introduces SlipSense, a multimodal framework for low-latency and generalized slip detection in dexterous manipulation.
Utilizes a compact sensor (TacV5) combining a $32 	imes 32$ piezoresistive array (240 Hz) and a 3-axis MEMS accelerometer (8 kHz).
Addresses limitations in current systems regarding detection latency and cross-platform generalization in tactile sensing.

stories.title: Discrete Beckmann Transport Models for One-Step Language Modeling and Reasoning
stories.author: Shiyi Wang
bullet_points: Introduces Discrete Beckmann Transport Models (DBTM) as an alternative to traditional autoregressive language models.
DBTM aims to overcome limitations in diffusion/flow models, specifically the need for costly teacher model distillation for multi-step sampling.
The model is built upon a time-independent flow whose autonomous transport map has theoretical guarantees regarding point mapping.

stories.title: Bellman Policy Optimization
stories.author: Lidong Bing
bullet_points: Introduces Bellman Policy Optimization (BPO), a new critic-free method for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR).
BPO reformulates Policy Mirror Descent (PMD) for autoregressive generation using Bellman equations, avoiding intermediate state value estimation.
The research aims to improve the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) through this novel RL approach.

stories.title: Stellar Colosseum: A Many-Agent Harness for Long-Horizon Research in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science
stories.author: Vahab Mirrokni
bullet_points: Introduces 'Stellar Colosseum,' a new harness designed to manage long-horizon research problems in math and theoretical computer science using language models.
Addresses the current limitation of LLMs in producing reliable proofs for complex, multi-step research tasks.
The system employs mechanisms like exploring alternative strategies and a 'readiness gate' to guide the decomposition of complex problems.

stories.title: Disentangling Representation Evolution in Transformers through Directional Decomposition
stories.author: Shen Yan
bullet_points: The research models Transformer representation evolution as a functional geometry, analyzing learned additive transformations.
It decomposes these updates into parallel and perpendicular components, revealing substantial parallel components beyond simple residual paths.
The decomposition method is applied to analyze updates within both attention mechanisms and MLP layers.

stories.title: Verifiable by Construction: Claim-Level Evaluation of Verbatim Citation in Clinical Question Answering
stories.author: Michael Oberst
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in current LLM-based clinical QA: citations are often too broad for practical verification.
Proposes a novel approach where responses are 'verifiable by construction' using fine-grained, verbatim quotes.
Aims to significantly improve the trustworthiness and usability of LLMs in high-stakes medical environments for time-constrained clinicians.

stories.title: HypoEvolve: Genetic Algorithms Enable Multi-Agent LLMs to Discover Scientific Hypotheses
stories.author: Zhen Wang
bullet_points: Introduces 'HypoEvolve,' a framework using genetic algorithms to enhance hypothesis discovery in Multi-Agent LLMs.
The system allows scientific agents to synthesize evidence, assess proposals, and iteratively refine explanations.
The research aims to decouple the impact of agent scientific capabilities from the effects of their collaborative strategies.

stories.title: Inoculation Midtraining with Learned Neologisms
stories.author: David Demitri Africa
bullet_points: Introduces 'Inoculation Midtraining' to guide LLM learning during earlier training stages.
The technique uses a designated neologism (<quarantine_token>) to teach models to associate unsafe behavior with a specific context.
Aims to shape the generalization of desirable versus undesirable properties in LLMs before final post-training.

stories.title: OpenArm: An open-source 7DOF humanoid arm
stories.author: Lwrless
bullet_points: Introduction of OpenArm, an open-source humanoid arm project.
The arm features 7 Degrees of Freedom (7DOF), indicating significant robotic dexterity.
The open-source nature suggests community contribution and rapid development in robotics.
